content.rationale:
The commitment: `deccy draft <node>... [--edit <id>]` opens one draft for each node the call names — a node named twice opening two drafts — and for each it mints a fresh handle, creates a jj workspace of its own outside the repository at the path that handle derives under one per-user root, writes the draft's record `open` at `.deccy/work/<handle>.json` naming that node, that edit and that workspace, and returns one line carrying the handle and the workspace path, in the order the nodes were named. A call naming no node, a call carrying an argument the form does not name, and `--help` are answered by the argument surface before a store is taken, so a refusal leaves no workspace and no record and the help answers on a root-less context. `src/verb_draft.rs` is that commitment as Rust: `run(context, args)` is M-route's handler shape, returning its lines and its `Refusal` for the envelope to write.

The surface (szvotxpq, vnwmpwrx). The form is the invocation `draft <node>... [--edit <id>]` and nothing else: the node ids and the edit are this verb's own arguments. The list is not deduplicated, because the draft model counts drafts and not nodes and already permits one node several drafts; the handler therefore iterates the names in the order given and opens one draft per naming, which is what makes a node named twice yield two records, two distinct handles and two distinct workspaces. `--edit` names the one edit a record carries, and an omitted flag falls back to the edit the invocation is made in — the current working copy's change id, read through the runner — because the model gives each draft exactly one edit and an opening is not performed from nowhere. The report is the handle together with the workspace path: the handle is the record's key and the path is what the record's workspace reference names, so the pair is the record's own fields read back, and it is the smallest report that leaves each opened draft reachable. The line's exact text, separator and stream are not fixed here, only that it carries both.

The refusal and the argument surface (xzrkrmmr, qtqnuqxo). A call that names no node is refused at the argument surface, ahead of any reach for a workspace, and the same point refuses an argument the form does not name, naming it as evidence. Because parsing reaches nothing, the refused call creates no workspace and writes no record: the surface answers first, and only then does the operation take the store. `--help` is the same placement read outward: the verb carries its own line (xlvoxmyl, rwlywqrk) and answers it before the store is taken, so it answers on a context with no repository — a root-less directory resolves as a state and not as a resolution failure, and only the operation refuses when it needs a workspace.

The record and its state (kwqnrzoz, owyntkvw, vkkwusty, ooquotol). Each draft has exactly one record, keyed by the minted handle and named by it, carrying exactly one node, one edit and one workspace by name and path, plus its base. The record is not a node document: it has no change under `nodes/`, is not listed with the nodes and is not validated as one, so opening writes nothing into the graph and `nodes/` is byte-for-byte what it was. The state written is `open`, because a draft the call has just opened has landed nothing and `landed` exists only after a recording this verb does not perform. The write makes no operation: it appends no marker and is not bracketed, so `.deccy/markers.json` stays absent and undo and redo receive no unit of their own.

The base (zsvukpls, ttkuyvxp). The record carries a content identity for every path of the node's owned set, taken at the opening: the set is attributed through the ownership rule — the node document plus the paths an array `ref` lists, the document alone when `ref` is inline — each path's content is read at the change that owns the node, and `draft_identity::base` turns each path's bytes into that path's identity. The base is taken then because that is when the record first exists and when the workspace the draft is written in is created; a base taken later would describe content the caller never saw.

The workspace (xqzstoyo, lpkssxpp, tyoypkmp, pvnszwum). The working copy is created outside the repository, under one per-user root, at the repository's namespace under that root plus the record's handle, and nothing is appended. It is created at the change that owns the named node (pvnszwum): a working copy is always a copy of some revision, and the record's base describes the node's owned set as it stands at the change that owns the node, so the verb passes that change id — the id it read the node document with — to `jj_workspace::add`, making the working copy hold exactly the content the base records instead of whatever the invocation's own change happens to hold. Created at any other revision, the workspace would hold content the base does not describe while the base describes content the workspace does not hold, which is the disagreement the base exists to catch, moved from the landing to the opening. The root is one directory per user; the namespace is derived from the trunk root the store is opened on alone, which is the repository's own root rather than the invocation workspace's, so two repositories' drafts sit under different namespaces of one root and one repository reaches the same namespace from any of its working copies; the handle keeps two drafts of one repository apart. The creation runs through the workspace seam, `jj_workspace::add` over the caller's `Jj`, so nothing here searches PATH and a jj refusal surfaces as a value carrying its evidence. The jj workspace's name is the caller's and is recorded as the workspace's name, so `jj workspace list` names the record's path under the record's name. The literal per-user root and the namespace's spelling are the implementation's: no recorded prerequisite fixes them, and the derivation is the part that is fixed.

The handle and the registry (upuuwzmr, rroqqrzq). The handle is minted fresh for each draft, independently of the draft and the graph, and redrawn while a record already holds the candidate — the freshness predicate is the existence of the record file the handle names. The workspace path follows from the handle, so the verb mints before it creates the directory, and the record's key and the directory's name are one token with no naming step between them. The record is stored through the registry at the path the handle names, one document per handle, checked against the carried record form before it is stored.

The state root (mrwtusss, lotlstzr). The store is taken through the context's state accessor rather than through its trunk-only one, so it is the store on the repository's trunk root from whichever working copy the call runs in, and both places the opening writes or names follow from that one root: the registry is the trunk root's `.deccy/work`, so it is the repository's one registry and a draft opened from a linked workspace is filed with the repository's drafts instead of into the linked workspace's tree; and the namespace is derived from that same root, so the draft lands under the namespace a trunk invocation takes. Opening writes no graph state and appends no marker (ooquotol), so it is not one of the invocations the trunk-only door (mrwtusss) refuses, and the verb keeps opening outside the trunk; the accessor's own refusal still answers a context with no resolved workspace, and the verb's surface, its refusals and its record shape are unchanged by this.

The order (qxuzyvsr). The workspace is created before the record is written. The record is a claim about the working copy its workspace reference names, so a record written first would assert a directory the draft is not in; and because the registry is the documents that are there, never writing the document means no record survives a failed open. With the repository's namespace unwritable the creation refuses and no record is written; a workspace left behind by that failure is not something the scan can see, so whether it is removed is not decided here.

The handler and its shape (ynvwvzrm, zttrwlts, popowxnw, utrzvyyt). The handler is M-route's shape, `fn(&Context, &[String]) -> Result<Vec<String>, Refusal>`, so the dispatcher's `draft` row compiles and the context is injected rather than reached for; every failure is a `Refusal` value carrying its evidence and is rendered by nothing here; the lines are returned for the envelope to write, and the module prints nothing. The module is the single flat file `src/verb_draft.rs` (szmuyqrq), and the gate that drives it is a self-contained test crate (knqkxzns).

What is left open. The literal per-user root, the namespace's spelling and the jj workspace's name are implementation choices that no prerequisite fixes. A named id that names no node has no owned set to read, so the opening refuses with the id as evidence; the surface leaves that case to a commitment of its own, and this node settles no wording or status for it. The refusal's rendering and exit status, the exact line text beyond the handle and the path, and whether a failed workspace is removed are not decided here either.
